title: CLR/20/2013 of RAM MULAKH DARBAR DIVYA YOG MANDIR and ANOTHER Vs MADAN LAL ALLEGED PROFESSOR M. LAL MAHARAJ and ANR

paras.text:
CLR No. 20 of 2013
Hon'ble Manoj K. Tiwari, J.
Mr. Siddhartha Singh, Advocate for
the revisionists.
Mr. Arvind Vashishta, Senior
Advocate, assisted by Mr. Vivek Pathak,
Advocate for respondent no. 1.
Heard learned counsel for the
parties.
This Civil Revision has been filed
under Section 115 Code of Civil Procedure
against the order dated 01.02.2013 passed
by learned Civil Judge (Senior Division),
Haridwar, whereby revisionist's application
seeking withdrawal of the suit with liberty
to file fresh one was partly allowed and the
suit was dismissed as withdrawn,
however, liberty to file fresh suit was not
granted.
According to learned counsel for the
revisionist, revisionist filed a suit for
declaration and injunction in the year
1999. In the year 2003, revisionist filed
an application seeking leave to amend the
plaint, which was allowed vide order dated
16.12.2004, however, revisionist could not
incorporate the amendment within the
stipulated time. Consequently, he filed an
application seeking extension of time to
incorporate the amendment. His
application for extension of time was
rejected. Subsequently, on 24.01.2013,
petitioner filed an application under Order
23 Rule 1 C.P.C. seeking permission to
withdraw the suit with liberty to file fresh
suit.
Learned trial Court allowed the
prayer for withdrawal of the suit and the
suit was dismissed as withdrawn vide
order dated 01.02.2013, however, liberty

to file fresh suit was refused. The reason
assigned for refusing the liberty is that
plaintiff (revisionist herein) could not point
out any formal defect in the suit which
may warrant withdrawal of the suit with
liberty to file fresh one.
Learned counsel for the revisionist
submits that the impugned order passed
by trial Court is unsustainable, inasmuch
as, learned trial Court either could have
allowed the application in toto or could
have rejected both the prayers made in the
application, and it was not open to the
trial Court to grant prayer for withdrawal
of suit only and refuse the prayer seeking
liberty to file fresh suit. In support of this
contention, learned counsel for the
revisionist relied upon a judgment
rendered by Hon'ble Allahabad High Court
in the case of Jai Prakash Vs. Rajendra
Prasad and others, reported in 2007 (66)
ALR 145. Paragraph nos. 7 & 8 of the said
judgment are extracted below:
"7. Further in the opinion of the Court,
the trial Court could not split the
prayer of the defendant in two parts.
The relief claimed by the plaintiff was a
composite relief, namely, withdrawal of
the suit with a liberty to file a fresh
suit. This relief cannot be split up by
the trial Court in two parts. The
application has to be allowed in toto or
has to be rejected in toto. The Court
has no Jurisdiction to split up the
relief in two parts unless the plaintiff
gives his consent to that effect.
8. In Balbir Singh v. Smt. Sulochana
Devi , this Court held that the Court
could have accepted the application
under Order XXIII, Rule 3 or rejected it
in toto but could not split up the

prayer to grant one relief and refuse
the order relief."
Per contra, learned Senior Advocate
appearing for respondent no. 1 supports
the order passed by trial Court. He
submits that there was no formal defect in
the plaint which may warrant grant of
liberty to the plaintiff, therefore, learned
trial Court was justified in granting half of
the relief as sought by the plaintiff in his
application.
Learned Senior Counsel appearing
for the respondent no. 1 has placed
reliance upon judgment dated 19.09.2019
rendered by a Co-ordinate Bench of this
Court in Second Appeal No. 140 of 2019.
I have gone through the judgment
relied upon by learned Senior Counsel for
the respondent no. 1. Facts of the said
case are distinguishable.
Dismissal of the suit of revisionist as
withdrawn without grant of liberty to him
to file fresh one would non suit him.
Endeavour of the Court should be to
decide cases on merits and not on
technicalities. This Court is of the opinion
that learned trial Court could have either
allowed both the prayers made by the
plaintiff in his application or would have
disallowed both the prayers so that
plaintiff could have pursued the suit on
the basis of the plaint, as was filed.
Since the plaintiff/revisionist had
sought a composite relief, namely,
withdrawal of the suit with liberty to file
fresh one, this relief could not have been
segregated by the trial Court. The
application has to be allowed in toto or
rejected in toto. In my view, learned trial

Court was not justified in allowing
revisionist's application without granting
liberty to file fresh one.
In such view of the matter, Civil
Revision is allowed and the application
filed by the revisionist before trial Court is
allowed in toto. Consequently, he shall be
at liberty to file a fresh suit.
All pending applications stand
disposed of.
 (Manoj K. Tiwari, J.)
Arpan 05.03.2020
